about: The lake's events after position 7 of `log/`, each following the one before it without a gap, in the one format like every other line. `shows` names what a line is there to show, and each verifier holds one check for each name. `misplaced` holds lines that are not of the lake: each stands at its position after the event before it, its hash made right, and breaks one rule for where a member sits, so a reader refuses it for that alone.

events.about: A `migrated` event that re-keys `account` from `number` to `iban`, moving key `7` to `DE%3A01`: a `:` in the new key is percent-encoded (§2.3).
A record ingested with `upstream`, the lake and position its values were read from (§1.1). The member is not in the event's id (§3).
A `declared` type whose derived field calls `date_bucket` (Appendix B).
A `write_proposed` whose write is `declare`, a set of declarations (§2.4).
A `write_proposed` whose write is `migrate`, a migration with the report its preflight answered (§2.4).
A `declared` type carrying `annotations` on the type, on two fields and on a relation. Its schema hash is the one the same type without them hashes to: annotations are not shape.

A `declared` type whose relation `shelf` is derived from its `shelf_code` matching the target's `code`. Its schema hash is the one the same type with the relation carried by link records hashes to: `derived` is not shape.
A `declared` trigger with `max_depth` 1.
A `declared` trigger on `slip` whose guard is `retired()`, so it fires only when a write retires a slip (Appendix B).
A `declared` view over `slip` that counts the slips on one shelf, the shelf a read binds as `shelf`: a view's `params` and a call of `param` (Appendix A, Appendix B).
A `declared` verb `print_slip` on the type `slip` (`scope: type`).
The `verb_called` of `print_slip`, which carries no `key`.
A `declared` view `shelf_load` that counts the slips on each shelf and merges `shelf`, counted by its `code`, on the same key (Appendix A).
A `declared` value type `slip_state` over three states (Appendix A).
A `write_proposed` whose write is `migrate_value_type`: `slip_state` over two of its states, with the report its preflight answered.
A `declared` type `loan` whose derived field `days` is `floor((back_on - out_on) / 1d)`, the whole days between two instants: a call of `floor` (Appendix B).

A `declared` type `shift` whose derived field `week` is `date_bucket(on, 7d, '2026-01-05T00:00:00Z')`, the start of the window of seven days from a Monday: a call of `date_bucket` by a width (Appendix B).
A `declared` object set `long_loans` whose `where` is `in_set('lent') and days > 30`: a call of `in_set` (Appendix B). The vector holds the line, not a lake that declares `lent`.
A `migrated` event of `loan` whose migration names a relation's rename, `relation_renames`, from `lent_to` to `borrower`: the relation keeps its edges (§2.3).

A `record_upserted` of the `sys.setting` `view_kept.loan_days`, which asks for the view `loan_days` to be kept. It is the setting's first version, so it carries `made`. The vector holds the line, not a lake that declares the view.

A `record_upserted` of the `loan` `l1` at `version` 4 that carries `made`: the write found no live record under the key, and a version above 1 says the record was retired before and is made again (§2.3). The vector holds the line, not the three events before it.

A `write_proposed` whose write is a migration of `loan` that declares `out_on` `sensitive` and changes no stored value: its preflight's report holds `restated`, what `to` states otherwise than the declaration in force (§2.4).

events.about: A `declared` type `ticket` whose required field `state` declares `initial` `new`, the value the fold fills where a write makes a record and gives the field none (§2.2, §2.3).

A `declared` function `loan_days` that carries `with_the_set`: another declaration of the same set follows in its append, and the records the set computes again are computed once, at its last declaration (§2.3). The vector holds the line, not the set's last declaration, so these are lines and not a log a fold accepts: a log that ends inside a set is damaged.
A `value_type_migrated` that renames `lent` to `out` in the records of `loan` (§2.2).
A `write_proposed` of a `migrate_value_type` that carries `renames`, with its report's `renamed` counts (Appendix A).
A `write_proposed` of an upsert, `pinned`: its proposer's grant admits only some records of `claim`, so its accept is refused once the record or the type changed after it (§2.4).
A `declared` type `due` whose field `on` is of the kind `date` (§1.3, §5).
A `declared` value type `pay_day` over the kind `date`.
A `record_upserted` of `due` holding the date `2026-07-05`: a value is a string.

An `output_recorded` of a function backing that carries its `output` and fills `due` `d1`'s `day` (§2.5). The records and the function are not declared in the vectors: a reader of the format checks members and hashes here, not the fold.
A fill of the same call (the same `seam` and `input`) for `due` `d2`, which names that output by `output_at` and carries none (§2.5).

A `lake_upgraded` from format 16 to 17 (§6), as a writer's open appends it right after its `lease_taken` where the lake's newest event was in 16. It stands here to show its members alone: in a whole lake it follows events of the format before, which this lake of one format does not hold.
A `declared` type whose `email` is declared `erasable` (058): a source's values of it enter the log sealed under that source's key.

A `record_ingested` whose `sealed` names the key `1` of its source and the member `email`, which the patch holds as the base64 of AES-256-GCM-SIV over the value's canonical bytes (§1.4); its id is made from the patch as stored. The vectors' key is SHA-256 of `lakelands:vectors:key`.
A recorded output computed from `crm`'s erasable value: `sealed` names the key and the source, the `output` is sealed, and the `input` is an HMAC under a key derived from the source's (§1.4).

A `declared` object set whose `where` reads across an edge: `shelf.capacity`, through the derived relation `shelf` onto the shelf's key (`docs/decisions/055-a-path-steps-through-a-reference.md`), a form format 16 holds and 15 does not.
A `declared` trigger whose `when` reads across an edge and asks `exists` of the derived relation: `exists(shelf) and shelf.capacity > 10` (055), a form format 16 holds and 15 does not.

A `declared` type `payment` with two constraints (`docs/decisions/059-a-type-declares-its-constraints.md`): `never_overpaid`, which admits at ingest, and `closed_stays`, which reads `previous` and refuses at ingest by default, a form format 16 holds and 15 does not.

events.about: A host forgot `crm`: its key's version `1` is destroyed, and every value it sealed folds as erased, before this position and after (§2.3, 058).

A `declared` type `parcel` whose `state` only its verbs write (`authority: verb`, lakelands#1130), with an `initial`: `upsert` and `ingest` are refused it, a verb's `set` writes it. A form format 17 holds and 16 does not.

A `declared` setting `vat_rate` of the host (063, extended, lakelands#996): a `decimal`, with its unit, its meaning and its group `operator`. Every write of `vat_rate` is judged as a write of a decimal field. A form format 17 holds and 16 does not.

A `record_upserted` of the `sys.setting` `vat_rate` carrying the `group` the store stamps from its declaration, which a grant's `only` on `sys.setting` names. A member format 17's `sys.setting` holds and 16's does not.
A `write_proposed` whose `declare` carries its plan: per type it would compute again, the records computed again and those it would leave naming no live record (062).

A `record_ingested` of `erp` in the delivery `batch-7`, the id its caller gave the `ingest` (§1.1): every record of that call carries it, and its id is made without it (§3), so the same record delivered again under another delivery is a duplicate. A form format 17 holds and 16 does not.
A `declared` function of the backing `http` that declares `risk: high`: a call it makes due is proposed, and made when accepted (§2.3, 064).
A `declared` type whose field `notice` is computed by `notify`, the function declared at position 53 (§2.3).
A `record_upserted` of that type, which makes the call of `notify` due: the write the next line names as its cause (§2.4).

A `write_proposed` the store appended for the call of `notify` that the write at position 55 made due, as its writer: the record, the field its output fills and the call's digest on that record as that write made it (§2.5, 064). It holds no inputs: they are the record's, which a source's forgetting may have erased (058).

events.about: A `declared` withdrawal of the trigger `shelved` (lakelands#1219): from this position on it is not in force, and a read as of before still sees it; its version, 2, follows the declaration it withdraws, and a later declaration of the name takes 3. A form format 17 holds and 16 does not.

A `declared` type `voucher` whose records only its verbs retire (`retired_by: verbs`, lakelands#1148): `retire` is refused it, a verb whose effect is `retire` retires one. A form format 17 holds and 16 does not.
A `declared` verb `redeem` whose effect is `retire` (lakelands#1148): its call retires the record it is called on, under its `requires`. A form format 17 holds and 16 does not.

A `declared` trigger whose guard reads `created()`, strict, firing on authored writes and ingests alone and binding its reactions to depth 1: `when_strict` and `on_changes`, members format 17 holds and 16 does not (lakelands#1215, lakelands#1217).
A write that makes the slip `S-1`, which fires `slip_made` (§2.5).

A `trigger_fired` of `slip_made`, whose guard `created()` held, saying the write at its cause was an authored write that made the record: `change` and `created`, members format 17 holds and 16 does not (lakelands#1217).
A host's reaction to `slip_made`'s firing, one deeper: its context is reactive at depth 1 and its cause the firing. It makes the slip `S-2`.
A `trigger_dropped` in place of `slip_made`'s firing: the write at its cause is at depth 1, the trigger's `max_depth`, so a reaction to it could write nothing. A kind format 17 adds (lakelands#1216).

A `declared` function whose input states no `type` (lakelands#933): a type binds it as a field of any kind, and the function reads the value in the kind that type holds it. A form format 17 holds and 16 does not.

misplaced.about: A `record_retired` carrying `upstream`: a reader refuses it, since only a `record_ingested` event carries the member (§1.1).
Position 13 with `cause` written inside `context`: a reader refuses it, since a host's cause is the envelope's (§1.1).
Position 39 carrying both `output` and `output_at`: a reader refuses it, since a fill carries its output or names it, never both (§2.5).
`sealed` on an event that is neither a `record_ingested` nor an `output_recorded`, which a reader refuses.
`delivery` on an event that is not a `record_ingested`, which a reader refuses.
